content.value_statement: Lapsed subscribers hurt deliverability and retention when campaigns continue without rules. This skill designs a cohort definition, offer ladder, re-consent step, and suppression handoff.
actual_capabilities: Defines lapsed email cohorts by no-open and no-click windows.
Builds staged win-back ladders with timing, triggers, and stop rules.
Specifies the action that re-affirms opt-in for recovered subscribers.
Sets terminal sunset and suppression outcomes for non-responders.
Prepares handoff facts for consent, nurture, and preference owners.
Labels source data as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
limitations: It does not compute EQS or enforce final email quality vetoes.
It does not own the permanent consent or suppression record.
It needs a lapsed-window definition or enough data to infer one.
It does not design broad lifecycle flows like welcome or cart recovery.

use_cases.title: Recover dormant subscribers
use_cases.description: Create a structured win-back ladder before moving subscribers back into active nurture.

use_cases.title: Clean an unengaged list tail
use_cases.description: Define sunset rules that suppress non-responders without deleting recoverable subscribers too early.

use_cases.title: Run a re-permission sweep
use_cases.description: Plan the opt-in confirmation step and route consent facts to the system of record.

prompt_templates.title: Start a win-back plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known lapsed window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a win-back campaign for subscribers with no opens in 120 days on Klaviyo. We can offer 15% off.

prompt_templates.title: Design re-permission steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on consent renewal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a re-permission sweep for 18,000 inactive subscribers. Include the confirmation action, timing, and suppression rule.

prompt_templates.title: Map a sunset policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with partial engagement data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this engagement export summary to define lapsed segments, ladder steps, complaint guardrails, and terminal sunset outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare owner handoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the reactivation plan and handoff facts for consent-registry, email-sequence-designer, and preference-frequency-manager.

output_examples.input: No opens in 90 days, no clicks in 180 days, and no incentive available.
output_examples.output: A three-step ladder: soft check-in, preference confirmation, and last-chance notice. Non-responders are suppressed after seven days.

output_examples.input: Mailchimp export shows rising complaints and a large inactive segment.
output_examples.output: A measured cohort definition, capped touch frequency, complaint guardrails, and a sunset branch for subscribers who do not re-confirm.

output_examples.input: The re-permission program is ready for operational handoff.
output_examples.output: A concise handoff listing the re-consent action, timestamp owner, recovered path, suppression path, and open data gaps.

best_practices: Confirm consent status before designing any reactivation or suppression path.
Use measured engagement exports when available, and label estimates clearly.
Cap touches for lapsed subscribers and stop after the last-chance step.
anti_patterns: Do not loop inactive subscribers through repeated win-back attempts.
Do not enroll hard-bounced, suppressed, or unknown-consent subscribers.
Do not treat a simple open as renewed consent.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a reactivation plan with cohort rules, ladder steps, re-consent logic, sunset rules, and handoff facts.

faq.question: Does it send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. It designs the program and operational rules for use in your ESP.

faq.question: Can it work without an engagement export?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide a lapsed-window definition. It will label cohort details as estimated.

faq.question: Does it manage legal consent records?
faq.answer: No. It defines the capture step and hands the recordkeeping task to the consent owner.

faq.question: Which platforms can it support?
faq.answer: It can plan for common ESPs when you provide platform context and available export fields.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use another skill for welcome flows, final EQS scoring, consent storage, or preference-center design.
